recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement

lines.text: Kepler’s second law — the law of areas:

lines: The line joining a planet to the sun sweeps out
equal areas in equal intervals of time.
steps.why: The law says nothing about the shape of the orbit — only about how fast the planet moves along it.
common_mistakes: Saying the planet sweeps equal ANGLES in equal times, which is false for an ellipse.

recall.must_convey: That the line joining a planet to the sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time.
accept: line joining planet to sun sweeps equal areas
reject: d A by d t is constant

steps.memory_tip: The law of AREAS — the name gives you the quantity that stays constant.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the whole sentence: the line to the sun, equal areas, equal times.

steps.label: What it means
lines: So a planet moves FASTER when it is nearer the
sun and slower when it is farther away. The law
is the conservation of angular momentum: the
sun’s pull has no turning effect about the sun.
steps.why: A force pointed straight at the sun can never exert a torque about the sun, so the planet’s angular momentum — and with it the areal rate — cannot change.
common_mistakes: Saying the planet moves faster when it is farther from the sun.

recall.must_convey: That the areal velocity d A by d t is constant, so the planet moves faster near the sun.
accept: d A by d t is constant

steps.memory_tip: Equal area with a shorter radius needs a faster planet. That is the whole consequence.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. dA/dt = constant, then the faster-when-nearer sentence.
